planted_anomaly_detections.notes: half_written_file: a truncated 1700-byte CUSTBILL_CNVINGEST_003 (as .part and as a marker-less .dat) present in the drop during live run 392843989649812 was neither landed nor registered. stale_lock_file: the legacy 'lock file present ... continuing anyway' path does not exist in the converted unit; mutual exclusion is max_concurrent_runs=1 with queueing, demonstrated by runs 162539038705856 / 503264318851998. trailer_count_mismatch is a declared coverage_gap in the contract (record-content reconciliation belongs to dbx-parse) and was not attempted.

unverified_paths: Live SFTP transport: the drop directory was populated over the Databricks Files API from the legacy incoming/ bytes; no run used the dockerised SFTP fixture (make legacy-sftp-up) as the upstream source, so the sender-side upload path is verified only in the .part-then-final form this unit emits

A genuinely concurrent writer racing the reader was not simulated: atomicity is proven by the completion-marker protocol and a pre-staged truncated file, not by a real in-flight transfer during the exact moment of a job run

Terraform jobs_ingest.tf was validated only with terraform init -backend=false and terraform validate; no plan/apply was run against the workspace (parent owns shared state), so the live job was created by the CLI path and Terraform/CLI parity is asserted by matching settings rather than by an applied plan
Invalid-byte tolerance (encoding_policy.invalid_bytes) is covered by the byte-transparent implementation and local tests but was not exercised live with a deliberately invalid-byte payload
Downstream silver/gold behaviour, record parsing and the finance report totals are out of this unit's scope and were not reconciled here
